# SES Client

This utility file configures and exports an AWS SES (Simple Email Service) client instance, making it readily available for use in sending emails throughout the application.

## Overview

The `sesClient.js` file initializes an AWS SES client using environment variables for credentials and specifies the AWS region. This centralizes the email sending configuration and ensures consistent usage across the backend. It's a crucial utility for any feature requiring email notifications or communication.

## Parameters / Configuration

This file does not export a primary function that takes parameters directly. Instead, it relies on environment variables for configuration.

<ParamField name="AWS_ACCESS_KEY" type="string" required>
  Your AWS access key ID. This is required for authenticating with AWS services.
</ParamField>

<ParamField name="AWS_SES_SECRET" type="string" required>
  Your AWS secret access key. This is required for authenticating with AWS services.
</ParamField>

<ParamField name="REGION" type="string" default="us-east-1">
  The AWS region where your SES resources are configured.
</ParamField>

<Warning>
  Exposing your AWS access key and secret access key directly in the code is a security risk. Ensure these are stored securely in environment variables and never committed to your version control system.
</Warning>

## SES Client Export

This file exports a pre-configured AWS SES client instance.

### `sesClient`

The initialized AWS SES client object.

```javascript
const { SESClient } = require("@aws-sdk/client-ses");

const sesClient = new SESClient({
  region: "us-east-1",
  credentials: {
    accessKeyId: process.env.AWS_ACCESS_KEY,
    secretAccessKey: process.env.AWS_SES_SECRET,
  },
});
```

## Usage Example

This client is typically imported and used within other utility files or services that handle email sending.

```javascript
// In another file, e.g., src/utils/sendEmail.js
const { sesClient } = require("./sesClient");
const { SendEmailCommand } = require("@aws-sdk/client-ses");

async function sendWelcomeEmail(recipientEmail) {
  const params = {
    Destination: {
      ToAddresses: [recipientEmail],
    },
    Message: {
      Body: {
        Html: {
          Charset: "UTF-8",
          Data: "<h1>Welcome to our service!</h1><p>We are excited to have you.</p>",
        },
        Text: {
          Charset: "UTF-8",
          Data: "Welcome to our service! We are excited to have you.",
        },
      },
      Subject: {
        Charset: "UTF-8",
        Data: "Welcome Email",
      },
    },
    Source: process.env.AWS_SES_SENDER_EMAIL, // Ensure this is a verified SES email address
  };

  const command = new SendEmailCommand(params);

  try {
    const data = await sesClient.send(command);
    console.log("Email sent successfully:", data);
    return data;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Error sending email:", error);
    throw error;
  }
}

module.exports = { sendWelcomeEmail };
```

## Common Errors / Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Error: `Credentials must be provided`">
    This error indicates that your AWS access key ID and secret access key are not being properly loaded from environment variables. Ensure that `.env` file is present in the root of your project and contains `AWS_ACCESS_KEY` and `AWS_SES_SECRET` with valid credentials. Restart your application after updating the `.env` file.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Error: `Invalid parameter: Source`">
    The `Source` email address you are trying to send from has not been verified in your AWS SES account. You need to verify the sender email address in the AWS SES console before you can send emails from it.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Error: `SES is not configured in the specified region`">
    The `REGION` environment variable might be set incorrectly or SES might not be enabled/configured in the region specified ("us-east-1" by default). Double-check your AWS region configuration and ensure SES is available and set up in that region for your account.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>
